claimText: WHO officially declares green tea cures cancer

brave.title: Fact Check: WHO has NOT declared green tea cures cancer
brave.description: The World Health Organization has not made any declaration that green tea cures cancer. This claim has been circulating on social media without any basis.

brave.title: No, green tea does not cure cancer — here's what the research actually says
brave.description: While green tea contains antioxidants that may have health benefits, no major health organization has declared it a cure for cancer. Studies show modest associations at best.

brave.title: Reuters Fact Check: Green tea cancer cure claim is fabricated
brave.description: A viral social media post falsely attributes a cancer cure declaration to the WHO regarding green tea. WHO has made no such statement.

brave.title: Green tea and cancer prevention: What does science say?
brave.description: A systematic review of green tea and cancer risk. Some epidemiological studies suggest potential protective effects of green tea polyphenols, but evidence is insufficient to claim curative properties.

brave.title: WHO's position on traditional medicine and cancer treatment
brave.description: WHO supports evidence-based integration of traditional medicine but has never endorsed any single food or beverage as a cancer cure.
